newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil lower as futures nosedive,diffs sink.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil lower as futures nosedive,diffs sink.

text.p: NWE gas oil fell further on Wednesday as benchmark IPE futures fell and premiums sagged as demand continued to remain elusive amid healthy supply, traders said.
July IPE settled some $5.0 lower at 158.75 a tonne.
The heating oil barge market remained in the doldrums with premiums quoted at around July IPE -50 cents/+50 cents fob ARA for refinery material and -1.0/flat for storage material.
Trade was minimal with many players sitting on the sidelines while futures continued their downward track.
"Nobody wants to buy while it's heading lower," said one trader. "Business will pick up again when futures turn back up."
Low sulphur diesel barges were also quiet with premiums talked around the July +$5.0/+$6.0 fob ARA level.
The cargo market was also under pressure with substantial amounts of material in storage as a result of players having taken advantage of the recent low prices to stock up.
EN590 cargoes were fairly lively with a flexi cargo for first half July delivery trading at July +$5.25 cif NWE and another for July 1-10 delivery trading at July +$5.50 cif NWE.
A second half delivery EN590 cargo traded at August +$4.75 cif NWE.
The 0.2 percent market remained under pressure as buyers and sellers remained wide apart with bids and offers quoted at anything from July IPE +$2.0 to +$2.0 cif NWE.
Despite the morose nature of the northwestern European market, at least one low sulphur and two heating oil transatlantic cargoes were seen heading for the region.
